titleTag: The $250 US Visa Integrity Fee: Who Pays It and When
h1: The $250 Visa Integrity Fee: What a US Visa Actually Costs in 2026
deck: A second fee now sits behind the one everybody quotes, it is charged after your interview rather than before it, and whether you are asked for it today depends on which consulate you walk into.
metaDescription: The $250 visa integrity fee explained: who pays, when it is charged, which categories are exempt, why the refund is theoretical, and what a US visa really costs.
keywords: how much does a us visa cost
coverAlt: The $250 visa integrity fee is charged on visa issuance, on top of the $185 MRV application fee, taking a B-1/B-2 visitor visa to $435, with collection still uneven across consulates and no refund mechanism published

coverSpec.title: A B-1/B-2 visitor visa now costs $435 once the visa integrity fee is added
coverSpec.desc: The $185 MRV application fee is charged before the interview. The $250 visa integrity fee is charged on issuance, after approval, and is not charged if the visa is refused. It was created by the One Big Beautiful Bill Act of 4 July 2025, applies to almost every nonimmigrant category including dependents, and is reimbursable only in theory because no refund mechanism has been published.

faq.q: What is the $250 visa integrity fee?
faq.a: It is a fee created by the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, signed on 4 July 2025 as Public Law 119-21. It applies to almost every nonimmigrant visa category, it is charged when a visa is issued rather than when you apply, and the base amount is $250 with annual increases tied to inflation from fiscal year 2026 onwards. It is separate from and additional to the MRV application fee you already pay.

faq.q: Is the visa integrity fee actually being charged yet?
faq.a: It depends on your post, and that is the honest answer rather than an evasive one. The statutory start date was 1 October 2025, but collection has rolled out unevenly: practitioner reporting through mid-2026 describes some consulates charging it while others are still waiting on payment and tracking systems. Budget for it, do not assume you have escaped it, and follow whatever your own post tells you at the time your visa is issued.

faq.q: How much does a US visitor visa cost in total in 2026?
faq.a: For a B-1/B-2 the application fee is $185 and the integrity fee is $250, so $435 per applicant where the integrity fee is being collected. Some nationalities also owe a visa issuance or reciprocity fee set by their country's arrangement with the United States, which is separate again. A family of four is therefore looking at $1,740 before any reciprocity fee, flights or documents.

faq.q: Do I pay the integrity fee if my visa is refused?
faq.a: No. The fee is collected at issuance, so a refused application does not trigger it. The MRV application fee is a different matter: that is paid up front, it is non-refundable and non-transferable, and you do not get it back if you are refused. The integrity fee is the one part of the cost structure that is genuinely tied to an outcome.

faq.q: Can I get the $250 back when I leave the United States?
faq.a: In statute, yes, if you comply fully: no unauthorised work, and either departure within five days of your authorised stay ending or a lawful extension or change of status. In practice, no mechanism to claim it has been published. There is no portal, no form and no published instructions, and many visas are valid for years, so any claim would sit far in the future. Treat the $250 as spent.

faq.q: Who does not have to pay the integrity fee?
faq.a: Travellers entering under the Visa Waiver Program on an ESTA do not pay it, although the ESTA fee itself rose from $21 to $40 for applications filed on or after 30 September 2025 and then to $40.27 in January 2026. Diplomatic and official categories such as A and G are outside it as well. Everybody else applying for a nonimmigrant visa is inside it, including dependants on H-4, L-2 and F-2 visas.

faq.q: Does paying more get me an earlier interview?
faq.a: No. The integrity fee buys nothing at all in scheduling terms; it is a charge attached to issuance. The only fee that moves an interview date is the State Department's $750 expedited appointment pilot, and that runs only at designated missions, currently Mission Mexico and Mission Canada, and only for B-1 and B-2 applicants. Everywhere else, an earlier date comes from rescheduling or from a granted expedite request, not from money.
